overview: Qualitative interview study of readmissions within 30 days of hospital-at-home care, with three participant groups (patients, carers, clinicians) sampled around recent readmissions.
population: Patients readmitted within 30 days of discharge from the program in the study period (target 16), their family carers (target 10) and program nurses and physicians involved in the episode (target 10); purposive sampling for diagnosis (COPD, heart failure, other), living alone, time of worsening and language.
exposure: Readmission within 30 days after hospital-at-home care (the phenomenon of interest).
procedures: Eligible readmissions are identified weekly from the dashboard. A research nurse not involved in the patient's care invites the patient and carer within four weeks of the readmission; interviews last about 45 minutes at home, by phone or in hospital, with interpreters where needed. Clinician interviews follow the same episodes. A short structured summary of each episode is drawn from the record to anchor the interviews. Interviews are recorded, transcribed and analysed with reflexive thematic analysis by two analysts, one with nursing and one with patient-partner background.

outcomes.name: Accounts of the pathway to readmission
outcomes.measure: Themes from reflexive thematic analysis of patient, carer and clinician interviews
outcomes.timing: Within four weeks of each readmission
outcomes.why: Answers the managers' question of why patients return.

outcomes.name: Participants' views on avoidability
outcomes.measure: Themes on what could have prevented the return, by participant group
outcomes.why: Points to changes the program could make.

outcomes.name: Reach of the sample
outcomes.measure: Invited, interviewed and declined by group, language and living situation
outcomes.why: Shows who is missing from the accounts.

feasibility: About 36 interviews over five months at two to three a week, within the nursing lead's and one research nurse's time; transcription by the hospital's approved service.
biasMitigation: Interviewer not involved in the participant's care
Deliberate sampling of patients living alone and with limited English

biasFlags.label: Recall and self-blame
biasFlags.note: Participants may reconstruct events; the record summary anchors them.

biasFlags.label: Staff reluctance
biasFlags.note: Clinicians may fear blame; interviews are confidential and reported by theme.

flags: No quantitative outcomes; counts of themes are not reported as prevalence
parsimony.simplestPath: Three interview groups anchored to recent readmissions.

theoreticalFramework: No formal framework at the outset; SEIPS may be used during analysis to organise work-system factors if the themes call for it.
summary: Interview study of about 36 participants in three groups around recent readmissions.
